article.title: Shopping staples 30% dearer in Italy in 5 years
article.summary:
(ANSA) - ROME, AUG 31 - Italian shopping baskets containing food staples have risen in price by almost a third over the last five years, Il Sole 24 Ore business paper reported Monday.
The 29.5% gain is a rate far higher than the inflation rate recorded in the same period (21%), with peaks in the prices of vegetables (+39% for those most commonly used in cooking), coffee (+51%), and extra virgin olive oil (+47%).
This is according to a survey by Sole24ore, which found that tomatoes, one of the most commonly consumed products, cost 45% more, potatoes 44%, and eggplants 41%.
The Sole24ore basket is limited to 31 products, indicative of the weekly spending of a couple with one child.
Between 2021 and 2026, the price of this shopping basket went from 100 to 129.5 euros, an increase in line with food inflation calculated by national stats agency Istat in the same period (30%) but higher than general inflation (21%).

article.title: Italy population to shrink by nearly 4 million by 2050 as ageing accelerates
article.summary: Italy's population is projected to significantly decrease by 2050.  Birth rates remain low, while the elderly population is expected to grow.  This demographic shift will create new economic and welfare system challenges.  Southern regions anticipate the most substantial population losses across the country.  Immigration has previously helped stabilize the population figures.

article.title: Italy's population to shrink by 4 million by 2050, stats agency says
article.summary: ROME, Aug 31 - Italy's population will shrink by almost 4 million by 2050, undermining the sustainability of its economy and welfare system as the proportion of elderly people increases, national statistics bureau ISTAT warned on Monday.

article.title: Over 13 million fewer residents in Italy in 2080
article.summary:
(ANSA) - ROME, AUG 31 - Italy's population will continue to decline and age and it will have over 13 million fewer residents by 2080, Istat said Monday.
From 58.9 million residents on January 1, 2025, the population will drop to 55 million in 2050, the stats agency said.
In 2080, however, the number is expected to be 45.8 million: over 13 million fewer than today.
Furthermore, the number of couples with children is expected to decrease until it falls below those without children: from the current 7.5 million, 28.1% of the total, it will drop to 5.8 million in 2050, when they will represent just 21.1% of families. Childless couples, on the other hand, are increasing: from 5.4 million in 2025 to 5.9 million in 2050 (+8.8%). Their share of the total will rise to 21.4%. (ANSA).Read article...
